title: Window Sums
statement: Implement `solve(items, k)`. Return the sum of every contiguous window of length `k`. Windows step forward by one index. If `k` is outside 1 through the length, return an empty list. Reuse the previous sum: add the incoming value and subtract the value that left.
constraints: items is a list of integers
hints: The first window is the sum of the prefix of length k.
Each later window is previous + items[i] - items[i-k].

approaches.name: Sliding sum
approaches.explanation: Recomputing each window from scratch is O(n*k).

editorial: Recomputing each window from scratch is O(n*k). The sliding update is O(n) because adjacent windows share k-1 terms. The first window is the only one you sum from scratch.
